64.name: ROTATE_PLAYER
64.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary. Field 1 is an ANGLE IN RADIANS and field 2 is a normalised turn amount in (0,1]. Both are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says ([u32,u32], wire 10 bytes), so the typing here is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed' to float -- while their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS. (1) The client names the quantity itself: the public entry 0x008165C0 range-checks its float argument against the assert text `(rotation >= -1.0f) && (rotation <= 1.0f)` from P:\Code\Gw\Char\Cli\ChCliApi.cpp line 5562, then tail-calls the sender; that argument becomes field 2 (as its absolute value) and decides field 1's sign. There is exactly ONE site in the image that sends 0x0040 -- the 12-byte wrapper at 0x009207B0, found by enumerating all 174 callers of the channel send 0x007DCF00 and recovering the opcode immediate at each. (2) The +/-inf in field 1 is a literal SENTINEL, not a computed ratio: the sender loads +inf from .rdata 0x00948654 when rotation > 0 and -inf from 0x0094E538 when rotation < 0, and when rotation is exactly 0 sends atan2(current facing) with field 2 = 1.0. So an infinity means 'turning continuously, sign gives the direction' -- it does NOT rule out an angle, which is the inference that kept this opcode unnamed. 146.name: MISSION_MASK_REPORT
146.why: Sender 0x00852930, whose only assert is the client's own MsCliMsg.cpp:181 'missionMaskBytes <= MISSION_MASK_BYTES' @0x00852952 (cmp esi,0x70) -- MISSION_MASK_BYTES = 112, and all 20 wire samples are exactly 112 bytes. The bit setter is idiv 8 / 1<<(i%8), bounded by MsCliMan.cpp:368 'mission < MISSIONS' @0x008524B9 (cmp 0x378) = 888. Independent stdlib corroboration: areatable.py reads 888 consecutive AreaInfo records from the same build via two agreeing locators -- two instruments, one number. REFUTABLE AND EXACT: at every one of the nine steps in BOTH sessions the mask's set-bit SET equals the cumulative set of ids the server named in GAME_SMSG 0x019F, 18 of 18 set equalities. Not progress: the nine masks are byte-identical for two different characters of different professions three days apart. The per-mission u32's meaning and whether a bit means 'equal' or merely 'received' are open (0x0093 naming 146 while bit 146 is set contradicts the 'queue instead of set' reading). CAP RAISED 112 -> 116 ON 2026-09-13, AND THIS IS A FIELD CORRECTION, NOT A NAME ROW -- the first GAME_CMSG layout this file changes, so the evidence is given whole. THE TRIGGER: the first live capture on build 38888 (vault/captures/live/20260913T210901, Shing Jea Monastery, conn 10.0.0.210:63677) stopped framing its c2s stream at byte 31 of 1,303 on the fifth client message after the map load, `array8 count 116 exceeds declared cap 112`; the message is 120 bytes on the wire (u16 opcode, u16 count 0x0074, 116 bytes of mask) and GAME_CMSG 0x0093 frames cleanly immediately after it, so it is not a framing slip. THE CORPUS SAID 112 WAS RIGHT UNTIL THAT DAY: 160 c2s 0x0092 across every earlier live tape (builds 38797, 38833, 38849), 160 of them exactly 112 bytes, and 803 of 803 on loopback -- the cap held on every tape before 38888 and fails on the first tape of 38888, which is the signature of a client change, not a decoder defect. RE-DERIVED FROM THE 38888 IMAGE RATHER THAN RAISED TO FIT, three witnesses that share no premise, each with its 38797 control: (1) the client's SEND descriptor -- `msgshape.py 0x0092` on the pristine 38888 image (vault/client/2026-09-01_44fbd68767a8/Gw.exe) reads SEND table 0x00bcda80 cmds [0x92, 0x740b, 0x6] = array8[116], wire 4..120 bytes, where 38797's table 0x00bcb030 reads [0x92, 0x700b, 0x6] = array8[112], wire 4..116; the type nibble 0x0b is unchanged and only the capacity byte moved. (2) The sender's own bound: the MsCliMsg.cpp:181 assert site `missionMaskBytes <= MISSION_MASK_BYTES` is at 0x00852ea2 on 38888 and the compare feeding it is 0x00852e98 `cmp esi, 0x74` -- 116 -- where 38797's site 0x00852952 is fed by 0x00852948 `cmp esi, 0x70` -- 112. (3) The mission count that sizes the mask: both MsCliMan.cpp sites `mission < MISSIONS` (:368 at 0x00852a09, :409 at 0x008528c7) compare against 0x381 = 897 on 38888, where 38797's (0x008524b9, 0x00852377) compare against 0x378 = 888; and the stdlib `areatable.py` reads exactly 897 consecutive AreaInfo records out of the 38888 image, the same two-instrument agreement the original entry rested on at 888. RECONSTRUCTION, stated as such: MISSION_MASK_BYTES = 4 * ceil(MISSIONS / 32) reproduces both builds (888 -> 28 dwords = 112; 897 -> 29 dwords = 116), so the mask is dword-granular and nine new AreaInfo rows spilled it into a new dword. WHAT THE CAP MEANS ACROSS BUILDS: the codec's `length` on a counted field is an UPPER BOUND, never a fixed size, so 116 admits every 38797/38833/38849 tape (all 112) and the 38888 tape alike; the schema has no per-build dimension, and the number recorded here is the newest build's. messages.json keeps 112 because it is the byte-faithful OpenTyria import stamped validated_against_build 38797, where 112 is correct -- correcting it there would make that stamp lie. declared_unpack_size follows the same rule as GAME_CMSG 0x0045's array8[256] -> 262: header 4 + count 2 + cap, so 118 -> 122; the codec never reads it. VERIFIED AFTER THE CHANGE: the 38888 channel frames c2s 1,303 of 1,303 and s2c to its last byte, and every other live game channel still frames to its last byte. test_codec.py's LAYOUT_FIXED names this row as its fourth exemption, the only one whose correction is witnessed on the wire AND in the binary on two builds. RESOLVED 2026-09-14 (D13): a set bit means 'the server has NAMED this map's manifest hash to me' -- the mask is the client's acknowledgement of GAME_SMSG 0x019F MAP_MANIFEST_VERSIONS, sent after each batch, and it says nothing about completion or progress (the per-map dword is a download-manifest hash; 0x0093 [map] asks for the manifest when the client's archive lacks that hash). 0x0093 naming 146 while bit 146 is set is therefore not a contradiction: the bit records the naming, the request the fetch.

43.name: COMPASS_DRAW
43.why: OBSERVED for the mechanism, MEDIUM for the NAME, and the split is the point. Build 38797. THE MECHANISM: wrapper 0x00920230 writes the opcode as an immediate (0x0092024B `mov dword [ebp-0x50], 0x2b`) and asserts CharMsg.cpp:8129 `knotCount <= arrsize(message.knotData)` @0x00920262. That first dword is called `messageId` by the client itself -- SendMessage 0x007DCF00 passes it to 0x007DDE00, whose first assert is MsgChannel.cpp:392 `messageId < channel->m_sendMsgs.Count()` @0x007DDE15, indexing an 8-byte-per-id descriptor array, and 0x007DCFCA `or ax, cx` is where the 0x8000 game-channel stamp is applied. SOLE PRODUCER IMAGE-WIDE, established twice by methods that share no premise. (1) The wrapper has exactly ONE direct reference, thunk 0x00816110, which has exactly ONE caller, 0x008C08DC, and neither VA occurs as a stored dword at any alignment in ANY of the five sections -- so neither is in a vtable, and not even a runtime-built table could hold one, since the store's immediate would itself be in .text. (2) A value-first sweep that cannot desync: of 134 materialisations of 0x2b in .text across six encodings, exactly ONE instruction sits inside the body of a function that calls a send entry -- 0x0092024B -- swept over all 214 send call sites, which is the CORRECTED census (there are TWO send entries, 0x007DCF00 and the dword-array variant 0x007DCB10 with 40 sites of its own; the earlier 174 missed the second). Controls on 0x78/0x39/0x3d/0x2c/0x40 each find their producer, and 0x40 surfaces six candidates that separate on which slot the buffer's `lea` names, so the method CAN report a second one. Reachability of the call site was tested rather than assumed: reverse closure over 135,455 direct call edges from the enclosing function 0x008C0840 converges at depth 25 on NINE functions, all inside 0x008BA79D..0x008C0840, no Gm* module anywhere. FIELD 1 IS A CLIENT-ALLOCATED STROKE HANDLE, not a target and not an agent: it is [canvas+0xbc], written at 0x008C0065 either by popping the back of a recycle pool at [canvas+0x68] or from the post-increment counter at [canvas+0x98], and the client looks its OWN line up with the key {0, that handle} at 0x008BF427-0x008BF442. Two wire facts corroborate the allocator and rule out a colour or ping-type reading: our corpus emits 7 then 6 (a DECREASING pair no plain counter produces), and two flushes 250 ms apart that are one stroke SHARE id 6 while two separate strokes 250 ms apart differ. A server must ECHO it in GAME_SMSG 0x0091 field 2, never invent it. FIELD 2 IS A POLYLINE IN TERRAIN CELLS. Each u32 packs two SIGNED int16, LOW HALF = x: the pack is 0x00920280-0x00920291, and the encoder at 0x008C07F0 divides each world float by the double 96.0 at 0x0094DE10 -- the terrain cell pitch -- AFTER 0x008C0560 has added the player's own world position, so the value is ABSOLUTE world/96 and not an offset. The receive side multiplies by that same constant at three sites (0x008BF177, 0x008BE6C7, 0x008BE774) and sign-extends both halves with movsx at 0x0091EA60/0x0091EA67. THE WIRE DISCRIMINATES ALL OF THAT and could have refuted it: the client's own constants bound a compass click at sqrt(0.1650390625) * 11076.9228515625 = 4500.0 world units exactly (hit test 0x008C0130 vs the world scale 0x00BA0318), and the corpus's one live sample -- 20260807T143055 conn :60935 t=50.702, `[32811, 7, [3801175]]`, knot 0x003A0057 -- lands at (8352, 5568), 3236.4 units from the position the preceding 0x003D reports 150 ms earlier and 5.0 degrees off that message's own heading, while the three rivals (halves swapped 7140.1, unscaled 11562.4, unscaled+swapped 11580.7) are all OUTSIDE the compass. Eight further knots in vault/captures/authsrv/authsrv-20260805T214038-c2.jsonl carry a NEGATIVE low half, which under an unsigned read would sit 6.29e6 units away. RATE: knots accumulate at a 25 ms floor (0x008BF45E `cmp ecx,0x19`, and a faster sample UPDATES the last knot in place) and flush on a 250 MILLISECOND countdown (0x008C08B8 `mov eax,0xfa`), sending nothing when empty -- so a drag is at most 10 knots per message and the 16 cap is never approached. The unit is milliseconds on three witnesses: the clock is WINMM!timeGetTime (import at 0x009396F8 via 0x0046B4E0 -> 0x0047F730), the same delta is divided by the literal 1000.0 at 0x008C0877, and OUR OWN CAPTURES show consecutive flushes of one stroke at 0.251988 s and 0.249950 s. A single knot is a click (a ping), a run is a drag. WHY THE NAME IS ONLY MEDIUM: the SEND side names nothing but `knotCount` and `message.knotData`. The word DRAW is ArenaNet's but lives only on the RECEIVE side, in GAME_SMSG 0x0091's bound constant CHAR_MAX_DRAW_MINIMAP_KNOT_COUNT, and reaches this opcode by INHERITANCE through the descriptor pairing (0x2b's SEND cmds and 0x91's RECV cmds are identical but for one leading u16). `PING` is not the client's word for anything -- 0 hits across all 19,758 readable asserts -- so it is GWW's player-facing vocabulary and is deliberately not used here. Two rivals were taken seriously and refuted: hero-flag placement (CompassCanvas.cpp does carry :416 and :902 `aiFlag < AI_COMMAND_FLAGS`, but that path reaches NO send entry, and a flag order is one point where this is 1-16 packed pairs rendered as a polyline gated on `knotCount >= 2`) and target call (no agent id anywhere; the u32 comes out of a free list, and the client types it 0x404 rather than with its type-0 agent_id tag). NOTE the naming hazard: GAME_SMSG 0x002B is a DIFFERENT message, already named AGENT_UPDATE_SPEED, with 309 live occurrences -- any census not split by direction is wrong by two orders of magnitude. Evidence: 1 live c2s occurrence, 5 in vault/captures/gamesrv|authsrv as kind:"decoded" with name "?" (dated 2026-08-14; that tree is append-only and two of the five are from this arc's own working day), and studies/minimap/FINDINGS.md 4.1.

IT IS GAME_CMSG 0x002B PLUS A LEADING u16, AND THE u16 IS AN OWNER TAG WHOSE LOCAL VALUE IS ZERO. SO A REBROADCAST MUST CARRY A NON-ZERO FIELD 1 or the drawing client merges the echo into its own line and doubles the stroke. Nothing in the compass group resolves field 1 to an agent, a name or a colour, and the client types it u16 (cmd 0x204) rather than with its type-0 agent_id tag, so 'sender id' is RECONSTRUCTION about the number space and OBSERVED only as identity; what number space it draws from is NOT FOUND. Field 2 is the client's own stroke handle coming back (GAME_CMSG 0x002B field 1). Field 3 is the polyline: two SIGNED int16 per u32 with the LOW HALF FIRST, sign-extended by the movsx at 0x0091EA60/0x0091EA67 and multiplied back by the double 96.0 at 0x0094DE10 in all three consumers -- the exact inverse of the sender's divide at 0x008C07FB -- so knots are ABSOLUTE world coordinates in terrain cells and must be near the player to be inside the compass at all. A knotCount of 1 on a key with no existing line draws a PING RIPPLE instead of a line (0x008BE6B3 `cmp edi,1`) in the colour whose static initialiser at 0x00BFAC24 is 0xFFFF0000, opaque red -- which is what GWW documents a compass ping to be, and is the cheapest possible server-side demonstration. The bound is tight, no off-by-one, so CharMsg:4934 is unreachable from the network and an over-range send is INERT rather than dangerous -- it measures nothing. NAMING HAZARD: GAME_CMSG 0x0091 is a DIFFERENT, already-handled message -- `[u8, u8]`, 4 bytes, SEND table 0x00BCB030, bound in toolkit/authsrv/authsrv.py:980 as GAME_CMSG_INSTANCE_LOAD_REQUEST_ITEMS with a live dispatch arm. Different channel dict, one line away from a reader conflating them. Live count 0 of 22,524 s2c GAME_SMSG, which is expected rather than absent evidence: draws are party-visible and every live capture is a solo operator. 415.name: MAP_MANIFEST_VERSIONS
415.why: MEASURED 2026-09-14 over every live game connection in the corpus (18 tapes, builds 38797..38888; scratch join over deepwoundjoin.sequence + cmsgstream, written up in studies/divergence/FINDINGS.md D13). The ids are the maps the character can reach (the set grows across a character's sessions: 113 -> 137 -> 147 -> 158) and GAME_CMSG 0x0092's mask acknowledges exactly that set (18 of 18 set equalities, recorded on 146's row). THE DWORD IS A PER-MAP MANIFEST HASH, NOT PROGRESS: identical for two characters of different professions and across every session on one build for 193 of 211 named ids; 18 ids changed value with build 38888 and nothing else did (9 pairs of neighbouring ids -- 4/5/6, 176..179, 275/276, 359/360, 529/530, 537/538); map 787 alternates between two values across sessions on ONE build (a rotating map). What the value keys is the map's download manifest: a GAME_CMSG 0x0093 [map] request is answered by 0x0198 [phase] / 0x0196 [body bytes] ... / 0x0197 [3, map, hash] with THE SAME hash 0x019F named (136 requests, 138 replies, every asked id one 0x019F had named), and a freshly assembled run directory (a cold Gw.dat, 20260817T183323) asked for 136 of 137 named maps while the next session on it asked for none. Map 787 was asked for on every session whose hash differed from the previous session's (4 of 4 flips). 338.name: ITEM_SWAP_LOCATIONS
338.why: OBSERVED, binary and wire. Handler 0x00846840 (build 38797) resolves fields 2 and 3 as items by id (ItCliApi:2253 'item1', :2254 'item2'; an id indexes the item array at ctx+0xB8, bound ctx+0xC0) and the inventory by FIELD 1 through the inventoryTable hash at ctx+0xD4 (ItCliApi:2257 'inventory' -- the key a 0x0144 ITEM_STREAM_CREATE registered; ours is 1, retail's 116 / 241 / 1 per connection), then calls the ItCliInv swap worker 0x0084B020: both items must be IN a bag (ItCliInv:687 'item1->IsInInventory()', :688 'item2->IsInInventory()'), each is REMOVED from its bag/slot (0x84aeb0, ItCliInv:621/622 -- the remove worker 0x014B uses) and then ADDED at the OTHER's former bag/slot (0x849ea0, ItCliInv:105 '!bagParent->GetItem(slot)' -- the add worker 0x013E uses). The two items EXCHANGE LOCATIONS and nothing else is written; a hand changes only because a location in the equipped bag (bag type 2, slots 0/1) changed, the refresh any add/remove there fires. One extra rule, read to its asserts only: if either item sits in a type-4 bag (a storage pane), the OTHER item -- the one moving into it -- is first taken out of every equip set it belongs to (0x84a3a0, ItCliInv:348 '!(setMask & ~ITEM_EQUIP_SET_MASK)', :375 'set < ITEM_PLAYER_EQUIP_SETS'). Nothing in the handler is equipped-specific, so the W9 name ITEM_SWAP_EQUIPPED (medium, 2026-09-19, from the wire context alone) was too narrow and is retired here; the siblings are ITEM_CHANGE_LOCATION / ITEM_ADD_TO_INVENTORY. Fields [inventory key u16, item id u32, item id u32], 12 B, per msgshape (initializer writes) and messages.json. WIRE WITNESS vault/captures/live/20260919T103604 (RUN-WEAPONS-1A, agent 25): in every one of the four replies to c2s 0x0032 SELECT_WEAPON_SET, between 0x0148 ITEM_SET_ACTIVE_EQUIP_SET and the 0x006F hand writes -- [1, 212, 209] (axe out, scythe in), [1, 209, 210], [1, 210, 208], [1, 208, 212] -- field 2 the lead LEAVING the hands and field 3 the one ENTERING, 4 of 4, with no 0x013E or 0x014B for either lead (the shield's move is a separate 0x014B). Nowhere else in the 29-capture corpus. CONSEQUENCE for a sender: the leads ROTATE through the backpack slots (after one 0->1->2->3->0 cycle each inactive lead sits in the NEXT set's created slot), so a server must never name a lead's slot from its create; and because the add worker asserts the slot EMPTY, a shield leaving the hands must precede one entering (test_weapons 18 models these asserts). Sent by authsrv.select_weapon_set (WEAPONS-W9); the desk read is studies/weapons/PLAN.md 29.

None of those, nor the tester's one caller, reaches the AvApi dresser 0x007DFCE0, whose three callers are all ChCliApi message workers -- so the WORLD body follows the mode only through the server's 0x006E/0x006F (RECONSTRUCTION). Without this message the client reads an unsent zero: the circled bar on all four slots and a bare-headed doll in a town (ours, 20260923T185124). Our server sends [flags, 0xFF] right after its 0x00E9 (retail's position relative to 0x00E9; our burst sends 0x018E earlier than retail's), answers c2s 0x0057 with [value, mask] (RECONSTRUCTION), and sends an equip's 0x006F into a slot the mode hides here as item 0 (the fix pass); --no-visibility-status reverts. studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md 'The display mode'.
